answer: At the wharf where agents dock for paid work, each identity must hold a hardware-bound quill: a signing key that can issue only one sequential work proof at a time, so one machine cannot sign for many at once. The bond doubles for every extra identity sharing that hardware — 100, 200, 400, 800 — so ten clones lock 102,300 units. Their outputs are chained into a single sonnet of linked receipts and paid as one job, not ten. If any receipt is forged, the whole cluster bond is slashed. Cost grows exponentially with n while reward stays flat, so profit turns negative before ten clones.
